default_sources.albedo: de Pater, I., & Lissauer, J. J. (2015) for solar system planets and pluto
default_sources.k2_Q: Henning et al. 2009 (estimated); measured values body-specific
default_sources.star_age_Gyr: Connelly et al. 2012 (4.6 Gyr for all SS bodies)
default_sources.T_surface_K: Spacecraft measurements and thermal models; see DATA_README.md for per-body sources
default_sources.T_bio_K: = T_surface_K for non-ocean worlds; estimated ocean temperature for ocean worlds
default_sources.satellite_orbital_parameters: NASA SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements, accessed 2023-08-29.

Europa.T_bio_K: Adopted 270 K near-freezing ocean temperature; Lawrence et al. 2024 supplies pressure/salinity-dependent freezing context, not an exact measurement of this value

Enceladus.T_bio_K: Adopted 273 K near-freezing ocean temperature; Lawrence et al. 2024 supplies freezing context. This is not a hydrothermal vent temperature or a measured ocean mean

Triton.albedo: Nobis and Chevrier, 2025. Reports 0.67-0.86, taken as 0.77. Verbiscer et al 2022

default_sources.k2_Q_est: Henning et al. 2009 (rocky/icy: k2~0.3, Q~50 -> k2/Q=0.006; giants: k2/Q=3e-5)
default_sources.age_s: Stored duration 1.434888e17 s is preserved; it equals 4.5468856947 Gyr with the stored 3.15576e16 s/Gyr conversion, approximately 4.55 Gyr, not exactly 4.6 Gyr

exoplanet_data.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars, downloaded 2026-07-21 as recorded in exoplanet_data.csv header
exoplanet_data.stored_columns_note: The repository copy of exoplanet_data.csv is a column subset of the original NASA download, retaining all rows but only the 13 columns used by the analysis (pl_name, hostname, pl_masse, pl_rade, pl_orbsmax, pl_orbper, pl_orbeccen, st_mass, st_rad, st_teff, st_lum, st_age, sy_snum). Results are identical to the full table; the complete table can be re-downloaded from the NASA Exoplanet Archive using the access date and filter below.
exoplanet_data.tidal_energy: Calculated from planet's orbital parameters, does not consider any other tidal relationships (ie, moons, other planets)

frank_heating_rates.description: Frank supplementary Table S2 heat production per unit mantle mass (W/kg mantle) as a function of stellar age; the analysis applies it to total body mass as f_sil = 1.

radiogenic_isotope_params.half_life_sources: Per-isotope: U238/U235 from Jaffey et al. 1971; Th232 from Le Roux & Glendenin 1963; K40 from Beckinsale & Gale 1969
radiogenic_isotope_params.notebook_use: Decay constants (from half-lives) used in radiogenic energy integration; heating rates from Frank et al. lookup table

constants.source: CODATA 2018 unless noted; see constants.json for individual citations
